chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: Booker Pittman's family and Booker T. Washington connection
summary: Booker Pittman's family in Dallas: his mother Portia taught music at the high school, his father was a contractor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And by that time -- by that time Booker Pittman had become very proficient on his alto, and --
This is Booker Pittman, this is the grandson of Booker T. Washington.

This is the grandson of Booker T. Washington. In fact, he was named after his grandfather, Booker Taliaferro Pittman, and Mr. Pittman, who his father was, who married Portia Pittman, which was Booker T. Washington's oldest daughter, in fact, Booker and me were sort of in the crib together, because the families -- my family and his family was very tight.
His father was a contractor, building contractor, named Pittman. And he married Portia. Portia -- Portia was Booker T. Washington's oldest daughter, and she taught music

in the public high school. They named the school after Booker T. Washington. I went to Booker T. Washington High School in Dallas, Texas. And she was the music teacher. She taught voice, but she spoke seven languages fluently, because she had studied all over the world, Berlin Conservatory of Music, every place she had gone.

And she came back to Dallas and married, and had these kids. She had one kid, the oldest son was named Sidney Pittman. Then Booker was next, who was my age. And then they had one daughter -- what was the daughter's first name? Fanny, Fanny Pittman. Fanny was a beautiful piano player. The oldest brother, he went to Washington, D. C. later on in life and was working for the United States Post Office. He had an injury in his back and was like a vegetable. He became a vegetable, and was drawing a pension, and he was immovable. You know.
